summary: Forest-department campsite on the Ambika river near Waghai — riverside cottages, nature trails and an easy first taste of Dang's forests.
description:
Kilad is the gentlest of Dang's forest-department campsites: a nature-education campus on the Ambika river minutes from Waghai, with simple cottages and dorms under big trees, a riverside frontage, short interpretive trails, and staff used to school groups and first-time forest visitors. It was built for exactly that — introducing people to the forest without demanding anything of them.

Day visitors can walk the trails and riverbank; overnight guests get the better deal, with dawn birdsong, the river running steps away and Gira Falls, the botanical garden and Vansda National Park all within a fifteen-minute radius. Facilities are forest-department simple: clean, functional, generator-scheduled in places, and booked through the department's eco-tourism channels rather than hotel sites.

Monsoon is the full-immersion season — river high, forest dripping — while winter gives comfortable trails and the strongest birding.
highlights: 15-minute radius to Gira Falls, botanical garden and Vansda NP

modes.road: Just off the Waghai–Saputara road; signed approach
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn (~55 km)

timings.note: Day-visit window indicative; overnight guests per booking

fees.note: Indicative day-visit fee; cottage/dorm tariffs separate via booking

booking.notes: Stays book via the forest department's eco-tourism portal/range office; day visits walk-in

visit.notes: Carrying alcohol is prohibited on forest campuses; expect basic, clean facilities rather than resort comforts.

seasonality.notes: Monsoon for the river and green; November–February for trails and birds.

experience.photography_notes: River frontage at dawn; kingfishers and wagtails work the banks in winter.

amenities.food: Campus mess for guests when booked; Waghai town eateries otherwise
amenities.guides: Nature-education staff lead walks for groups; ask when booking

warnings: River currents strengthen sharply in monsoon — no swimming
Keep food sealed at night; the forest's smaller residents investigate

tips: Book ahead for monsoon and winter weekends — school groups block-book
Use it as a base night before an early Vansda NP or Gira Falls start

faqs.q: Can I visit Kilad without staying?
faqs.a: Yes — day visits to the trails and riverbank are allowed in campus hours for a small fee, subject to group bookings on site.
